description: A summary of one dataset computed on the server: one small row per group instead of raw rows. `agg` is avg, sum, min, max, count, or weighted_rate. To list observed values of a filter column, use agg='count', group_by=[<column>] (one value per row, plus its count); describe_dataset lists allowed enum values without a scan. `metric` is the figure to summarize (default: the dataset's key_metric; ignored for count). `group_by` lists columns to group by (year, code columns like district_code or county_fips, or category columns). weighted_rate is a population-weighted rate, SUM(numerator) / SUM(denominator) times the rate's per-N scale (1,000 for a rate per 1,000, so the figure reads like the rows' own rates; the value column's `rate_scale`), over the rows that publish both counts (`pooled_rows`; a row withholding its numerator is left out, not counted as zero); for a rate across several places or years it is the right figure, since avg averages the rows' rates without weighting by population. With `metric` set to one of the dataset's `pooled_rates` (a school zone's people per square mile), it pools that rate's own numerator and denominator. Takes the same `filters`, years, and `detail` as query_dataset, plus `order_by` ('value' for the summarized figure) and `order`. Each row has `<metric>_<agg>` (or `row_count`) and coverage counts (input rows, pooled rows, non-null counts), so suppression is visible. `aggregation_scope` says whether the source publishes rows at this level or they are recomputed from finer rows. A sum or weighted_rate across a column the dataset declares non_additive (overlapping rows) is returned with a `non_additive` block and a leading `non_additive_sum` advisory: that figure is not a total. NULLs are skipped. No SQL: every column name is checked against the dataset's schema.

NumericFilter.description: One comparison on a numeric metric; between includes both endpoints.

value.description: Finite bound for gt/gte/lt/lte, in stored units (0.9 for 90%).
value.title: Value

values.description: Ordered [lower, upper] bounds for between; omit value.
values.title: Values

NumericFilter.title: NumericFilter

detail.description: Level of detail, i.e. what one row describes: 'schools', 'districts', 'counties', 'tracts', 'states', ... (each dataset lists its own). Omit for the dataset's default.
detail.title: Detail

filters.description: Column -> value (or list of values). Keys are the code columns (district_code, school_code, county_fips, tract_geoid, demographic), the dataset's category columns, and a few lookup-table attributes (demographic_category, district_type, school_level, locale); describe_dataset's `filters` lists the exact keys and valid values. A list is OR; several keys AND together. A wrong key or value returns an error listing the valid ones.
filters.title: Filters

group_by.description: Columns to group by: year, code columns, or category columns. Omit for one overall row.
group_by.title: Group By

main_topic.description: Optional subject-area consistency check. Omit: globally unique topic names and full keys identify the dataset on their own.
main_topic.title: Main Topic

metric.description: Figure (metric column) to summarize. Default: the dataset's key_metric.
metric.title: Metric

numeric_filters.description: ANDed comparisons on numeric metric columns, before pagination or aggregation. gt/gte/lt/lte use value; inclusive between uses values=[lower, upper]. Stored units: 0.9 means 90%. NULLs do not match. describe_dataset lists numeric_filter_columns.
numeric_filters.title: Numeric Filters

offset.description: Number of rows to skip, for paging.
offset.title: Offset

order_by.description: Sort by 'value' (the summarized figure) or a group_by column. NULLs sort last.
order_by.title: Order By

topic.description: Dataset name, e.g. 'act_scores' (the last part of a key from list_datasets or search_datasets). The full key, e.g. 'education/gosa/act_scores', also works. main_topic is optional.
topic.title: Topic

year.description: Exact year. Use this or year_min/year_max, not both.
year.title: Year

name: aggregate
title: Summarize a Dataset by Group
